utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to you, sir. Would you please stand and read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Good morning. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. I believe Mr. Apostolski has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness Nikolce Grozdanovski.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: We know each other, but I would like to officially present myself. My name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, we are defending Mr. Tarculovski. Before I start my questioning, I would like to point out one thing. The two of us speak the same language, but I would kindly ask you to make a pause between answering and questioning, so that your answers can be translated in order that everybody the courtroom understand what we are talking about. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you give me your name, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: My name is Nikolce Grozdanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I was born on 11th of January, 1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me your marital status, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm married. I am a father of two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me if this is the first time that you speak about the events in Ljuboten and Ljubanci in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, it is not my first time. I have spoken twice, with the Prosecutor and once with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you were called by the Prosecution, did they tell you in which capacity they wanted you to speak?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. I just had a phone call through a colleague of mine, and I called myself, the Prosecutor. And when I came to see the Prosecutor, I was told that I'm in the process as a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you finish the conversation with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: When I was called the second time, I was told that I would be called again and that I should be thinking or recalling the situations, because I might be called again, but I was never called again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me about your education?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I have a university degree, meaning I graduated from the Military Academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When and where did you finish from the Military Academy?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I graduated the academy in Belgrade in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which department?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you ever been convicted?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I'm not a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you work now?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Now I am working in the crisis management centre as an official.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please explain whether that is within the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. The crisis management centre is a government institution and is not a part of the army or the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That means that you are not an army official now?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: That is correct. Now I'm not an army officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me when you left the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I left the army of the Republic of Macedonia on the 1st of October, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which position and rank did you hold then?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: My last duty in the army was artillery officer in the General Staff, and I had the rank of major.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether you had any combat experience during your army career?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I had combat experience. The first one being in Croatia in Koprivnica in 1991 and then in the Republic of Macedonia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you say "Republic of Macedonia," which period do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: My first combat experience was in March 2001, and then in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me, in the summer of 2001 what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the summer of 2001, since June, I was the commander of a mortar battery in the 3rd Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where was the 3rd Guardist Battalion stationed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The 3rd Guardist Battalion was stationed around the village of Ljuboten, on the foothills of the mountain Skopska Crna Gora.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction line 11 should be 3rd Guardist Battalion instead of Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me where your battery was stationed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The soldiers were accommodated in the children's rest house above the village of Ljuboten, and the battery's position was just above the children's rest room, near the monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: My immediate superior and the commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion was Major Despodov Mitre.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me who was the major's superior?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Major's superior, as well as my superior, was Colonel Blazo Kopacev.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where was the battalion's headquarters in the summer of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The headquarters was in the school in the village of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What kind of communication did you have between the children's rest home and the battalion's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: There was a wire communication and mobile phone communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you describe the wire communication setting and how did the communication function?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The links were set in a way that from the commanding post we had a wire that went to the children's rest home and in the rest home there was a station that divided the links towards the positions where the soldiers were. So all positions were connected with wire through the switch operating station and that is how we functioned. As pertains the mobile phone communication, we used them only in emergencies, whenever the need would arise, and sometimes the soldiers' families or relatives would call or the soldiers used them to call home.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your soldiers have mobile phones at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: At the time, not all of them had mobile phones. Very rare were the soldiers that had mobile phones because they were very expensive at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: We are talking about the year of 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. One mobile phone cost 600 Deutschemarks at the time and it was very expensive for a soldier to have a mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what kind of mortars your battery had at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: My battery had 120-millimetre mortars, M38 and M43.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What kind of range?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The range was 6.500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there any other mortars within the battery?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, there were other mortars as well. 82 millimetres. They were within the 1st infantry squad where Jurisic Mario was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have any optical instruments for monitoring?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. My battery had binoculars and artillery Busola. So the snipers were used for observing and for night observing we had one night binocular within the first companion [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where did you have the night binoculars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: It was on the Zdravec position. That is where it's located.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what observation posts your battery had at the moment?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: There was only one observation post on the location of Zdravec, and one reserve observation post on the position of Smok.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you explain to me in more details what your answer means?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: It means that in the positions Zdravec we had two soldiers that were on a shift around the clock, and on the position Smok we didn't have any soldiers. We only had wire communication because that was a reserve observation post. On Zdravec we always had soldiers that were continuously linked.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did I understand well that your battery had the Smok position as a reserve observation post?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Whose observation point was Smok?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The position Smok was the observation point of the 1st infantry company. They had their soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you, in the course of the day, have soldiers there, from the 1st Infantry Company?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There were -- there was -- this position was always manned, around the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me about the soldiers of your battery, whether they were regular soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. My unit was composed exclusively of reservists who were called in through the municipality to come in for duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have active officers in your battery?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I had one active officer. This was lieutenant Slavco Buteloski [phoen] and one -- and one other officer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the name of the officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How were your soldiers trained?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The reservists were persons who had served the army in the artillery department. Previously they had had experience in serving the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Once they came to you, did you organise any additional training?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We organised training to -- for the use of personal weapons and other tools. After the training they were taken to a firing range to fire with their personal weapons, and then they were taken to Krivolak so they can practice with the mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me the command system of your battery?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I was the commander. The lieutenant Slavco commanded with the mortar elements and the Sergeant Igor with the command path, that is to say, the units for the remaining sections. In the activity of the battery, I was at an observation point and I was in command of the fire and they were in the firing position and they commanded the soldiers which were at the firing positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How did this function in practice? How did you carry out the tasks within your battalion?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the need that we would open fire, we would -- I would go to the observation point and see where the enemy was and commanded from there, gave the direction where the fire should be sent. They were on the firing positions, and upon my command, they fired with their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your mortars, or were your mortars -- how were they positioned?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The mortars were positioned in three directions, each direction will -- had two mortars, one such direction was towards Crn Kamen, near the village of Brodec. Two mortars were aimed towards Bel Kamen. And one direction with two mortars towards the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So did I understand you well: You had therefore six mortars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, six.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have marked targets placed on your mortars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, each direction had a marked target. That is to say, benchmarks, which were visible and were -- and locatable on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which were these benchmarks towards Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We decided that these benchmarks which could be located on the map would be the church, the mosque, the mask -- the graveyard and the workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know where the last stop of bus number 57 is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There is at the end of the settlement Radisani, and there's an empty space there and this is where it is located, towards the beginning of the village of Radisani.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see from there the position of your battery and the mortars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. From this place it is not possible to see it, the position of my battery or to see the mortars. This is not possible from any position lower than the location of my battery, only from the higher elevations such as Zdravec and Bel Kamen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Why is it not possible for it to be seen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: It is not possible, because the mortars were in a valley. There were higher elevations above it. Therefore, it was not possible for this to be seen from lower positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it possible from any part of Ljuboten or the surroundings of Ljuboten to see the position of your battery where the mortars were?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. It was not possible at all to see my position from Ljuboten. From Ljuboten, we -- one could see only the 82-millimetre mortars and the cannons one located at the position Bomba and from the settlement Radisani, these could be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If your battery was active, is it possible to see from these position the position of your mortars, in view of the fact that when the mortar is active there is fire?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, it was not possible to see it, because these sparks, the fire that is emitted by the mortar, is within one half metre. So, once again, it is not possible to see it from lower positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can you tell us why your battalion was deployed in this part of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We were charged with the task to prevent the entry or advancement of the terrorists from the region of Matejce, Vaksince, and Slupcane towards Skopje. Our basic task was to observe and to prevent the entry of terrorists in the city of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you explain to us the general security situation in the region of the 3rd Guardist Battalion in the period of your coming until the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As a whole, I can say that it was fine, because we had no combat action. At the same time, the soldiers, on several occasions, were able to observe movements in the slopes above Ljuboten near Ljubotenski Bacila, towards the village of Matejce. Thus, on several occasions, they noted night movements of people and horses. Therefore, this part was not in very good order.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You had indications then above all for night movements?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Night movements was constant. Also, it was characteristic that vehicles from Skopje towards Ljuboten and in the other direction were noted during the late night hours. Also, in the area of Ljubotenski Bacila, during the night, we noted dogs barking which was a sign that there was presence of other persons there as well. Also, our patrols, which moved in the area above Ljuboten and Ljubotenski Bacila, oftentimes on the roads found bullets along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What did this indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This indicated that in this region there were terrorist groups who were moving from the village of Ljuboten towards Matejce and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the picture, 65 ter 178, N003-0425.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see this photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was most probably made from the Smok position.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us and to point the locations which you were just speaking about?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I see them here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Now the court usher will give you a pen. Can you please mark these locations?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The road where we had night movements of horses was the one I'm marking now. And they often used this road as well. The road by which one can go to Ljubotenski Bacila and then on to Matejce by car is the one which the soldiers used, and it's this one which I'm marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you now please with the number 1 mark the first road which you marked on the photograph, and for the purpose of the transcript indicate from where and to where this road leads.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This road leads from Ljuboten to Ljubotenski Bacila and then continues on to Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you now please, with the number 2, mark the second road, and could you tell us from where to where this road leads.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This road leads from the out-clinic in the village of Ljubanci up until Matejce and one can go on this road by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You marked yet another road. Could you now tell us, please, and mark this road with the number 3.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a road from the village of Ljuboten to -- leading to Ljubotenski Bacila.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you now please use an arrow to mark where Ljubotenski Bacila are [as interpreted] located?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Right here. There in a valley. They cannot be seen from here. There are hills up above. Therefore, one cannot see it, but they're in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you now please, next to this marking, post the number 4.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, the direction of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark this with the number 5.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And could you please mark the direction towards Matejce.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how you marked this with an arrow?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Matejce is over the hill. You have to go over the hill and go down towards Matejce. After the hill, a kilometre further down, is the village of Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you now please above this arrow which you drew and for the purpose of the transcript, mark with the number 6 the direction of -- leading towards Matejce.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, please, next to the road you marked with the number 3, we can see some houses, it seems. Do you see these houses?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see these houses. They're old and abandoned shepherds which, at the time we were there, were not operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark these shepherds with an X.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And place the number 7 next to them.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could, Your Honours, put this picture on 65 ter list, because this is a photo that we received from the Prosecution and we would seek to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The photograph as marked will be received as an exhibit. And the photograph will be added to the 65 ter list, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph will become Exhibit 2D85, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the photo removed with all the markings and then have the photograph shown without the markings. This is 65 ter 178, N003-0425. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You told me that this photograph was made from the position of Smok. Could you, in the left-side corner, mark with number 1, or where the position Smok would be?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Here, in the left-side corner, maybe more to the left or maybe to the right. But this is the position of Smok more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can one see other positions of the battalions on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- these are the positions of the 1st Infantry Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me first what are the positions?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Positions are Bomba, Mecka, Volk, and Zdravec.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to mark all of the positions with an X and please put a figure next to the Xs and explain what the positions are as you mark them so that it can be entered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is number 2, marking the position of Bomba. Point 3 is the Mecka position. Point 4 is the position Volk. Point 5 marks the position of Zdravec. Point 6 is a protruded point of the position Zdravec. And point 7 is a point of the position Zdravec number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark -- sorry, do you see the position Bel Kamen on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Not completely, but it is located in the upper right corner on the top of this hill, on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the position with an arrow.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Should I maybe put number 8?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, put number 8.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: So near the arrow is the Bel Kamen peak.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me which position had the best view to the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We had the best view from the position of Smok, because it was the closest point located above the village and we had a complete view of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to have this photograph on the 65 ter list and receive it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received and added to the list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit 2D86, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you regularly visited [as interpreted] the position of Smok?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. When I was doing visit to my soldiers, I frequently stopped to see the points of the first companion.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you describe how the position of Smok was organised, how it was prepared?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The position of Smok was composed of two parts: A bunker which was well equipped and well dug into; and a monitoring post which was located on the cliffs. Both were connected with a trench. A person kneeling down could move along that trench without being seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How long was the trench?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Not more than 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that you frequently visited the position of Smok. During your visits, did you observe the village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Frequently we watched the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: While you were watching the village, did you see some typical preparations for combat in the village, such as digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. We did not notice any fortification in the village. If we had noticed it, we would have reacted, but there was nothing like that in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If there had been preparations of that kind, they would have been immediately noticed from the position of Smok. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. If there had been any preparations at any point of time, the soldier would say have noticed it and reported to the commanding post.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you something concrete about the month of August, more particularly, the 10th of August, 2001. Do you remember what happened that day? We are talking about Friday, 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that day very well. There was a tragic event when eight soldiers died and other eight were wounded. It was a really gruesome event that shocked us all.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where were you when that happened?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I was in the rest house at the moment; I was having breakfast. And then the duty officer arrived and informed us that the truck hit a land-mine and the truck was used to transport soldiers from the shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What did you do when you heard that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I gave an order to lieutenant Slavko to go immediately to the fire position and prepare for action and to lieutenant Mario, I ordered to go to his positions together with his soldiers, and I also gave an order to my driver to get prepared and to get the jeep prepared and together with two soldiers and a medical person, I went to the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We went towards Ljubotenski Bacila, and around half an hour later, we stopped about 500 metres away from the Bacila because we were not sure, we thought we might be attacked, so we continued on foot, and after an hour, we arrived to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What did you do when you came on the spot where the mine explosion happened?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We were the first ones that arrived there, and we saw a shocking sight. The soldiers were scattered around. There were body parts scattered around and the sight was really horrible. We gathered the wounded soldiers closer to us so that they are not attacked. They were dehydrated. They asked for some water, and we were really sorry that we didn't have water with us and they were constantly asking for more water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I am sorry to interrupt. I'm just wondering, this -- the issue of the mine incident is an agreed fact. So I'm just wandering if my learned colleague could explain the relevance of this particular testimony at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The fact that is an agreed fact doesn't mean that it's not relevant. Carry on please, Mr. Apostolski, but of course you've no need to spend a lot of time on this, because there's no dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my intention was to connect the events in one series.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me if you gave any orders from that position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I ordered my unit to act in the area of Ardievi Bacila where the fightings were taking place at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: While you were on that position, did you have any phone calls?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, Mitre Despodov, Colonel Blazo Kopacev, General Sokol called me, they all called me on my mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you explain who General Sokol is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: General Sokol At the time was the commander of defence of the city of Skopje, and he was commanding all units in and around Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is his family name?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Sokol Mitrevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And when the two of you talked, what did General Sokol Mitrevski tell you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: First, he asked me about the situation and the incident, and then he gave me an order, if there was a need, to act, and to remove it from the position, because we were expecting a transport vehicle and we had to clear up the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What was your priority at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Our priority was to chase out the terrorists or to expel them from the forest, and we had the assistance of the combat helicopter that was flying above the forest at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What did you do afterwards?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: After some time, after 12.00, we had the transport helicopter and we put the wounded soldiers on the helicopter, and we loaded the killed on the truck and we returned to the rest house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When did you leave the position of Ljubotenski Bacila, where the mine exploded?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I think it was around 1.00 and then we went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where did you go back?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: First, I stopped at the position of Smok, because Major Mitre Despodov and Colonel Blazo Kopacev were there. I stopped at the position first to explain to them the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And where did you go afterwards?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Then I went to the children's rest house -- no, sorry. First I went to the mortar positions where I spoke with my soldiers, and after that I went to the children's rest house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What was the morale of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say that it wasn't very good. Everybody was sad and the morale was very low at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you meet with Major Mitre Despodov that Friday?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. First time, as I said, I met him on the position of Smok and then I met him in the school of the village of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What time was that when you saw him in the school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: It was about dusk, around 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what the two of you spoke at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: All commanders of the battalion companies were present at that meeting and we were giving a report about the situation. We reported about the soldiers that we received, what the current problems were, and we talked about the possibility that there were terrorists in the village and that we should be very attentive and prepared for any provocations.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In which village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, where you were on that Friday evening?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I was at the rest home throughout the whole time of that Friday evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, on Saturday, the 11th of August, 2001, where were you throughout the whole day? Can you describe to us what you did that day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Throughout Saturday, I was at my position with the mortars. We were training soldiers, since, on Friday, we received new soldiers and we had to train them how to use their personal weapons and the mortars. Therefore, the whole day, I was at my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On Saturday evening, could you please tell us where you were then and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I was at the children's rest home that Saturday evening, and nothing in particular happened then.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You did not notice anything unusual that Saturday evening?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. There was nothing unusual going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Now I will ask you questions regarding Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001. When did you get up on that Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, I got up at the regular time, around 6.00 a.m. This is my usual waking up time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And what did you do once you got up? What were your activities?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: First, I call in the command, and then the regular things. Preparing with the soldiers, starting from breakfast, change of shifts, the usual things.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you called in to the command can you tell us, please, what did you speak with them about?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the morning when we call in we report about the developments during the evenings, if there had been any changes. Since there were no changes, I reported that everything was in good order, and I did not receive any concrete tasks, nor did I have any particular comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did anything unusual happen on that Sunday morning?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Around 8.00 a.m. Major Despodov Mitre called me and ordered me to go to the Smok position to visit, and for the soldiers to be prepared to act and that we go to the positions where the mortars were. This was so because we heard sporadic fire from the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And when you arrived at the Smok position, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: When we arrived at the Smok position, the soldier in charge told me that there was fire from houses in front of the church to the left. There were several terrorists who were firing with automatic weapons, and from the Smok positions, we could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How could you see that -- that they were firing with weapons from there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We could see the fire from the weapons that they were using.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see them, and, if so, where?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I saw them, yes. They were a group of about four to five terrorists that were firing from the houses, near the church, in front of the church on the left side. It was characteristic that there was a wall there in -- there was a courtyard with a wall and they were firing from the wall, from the balcony, from the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you notice anything else happening then, when you were at the Smok position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. After a while, close to the Macedonian houses three mortar grenades fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown picture 65 ter 178, N003-0375.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell us from this position of Smok how did you make your observation? What did you observe with?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We observed with binoculars and artillery compass, and also there was a sniper vision.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please describe what you see on this photograph and whether you recognise this area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was also most probably made from the Smok position. And from here one can see the part of the village of Ljuboten around the church, if one can say this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark for us the location of the church. But, first, wait for the assistance of the court usher.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is where the church is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, the circle you just made was that of the church?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark this with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you circle the houses, if you see them, which you talked about earlier, and to mark them, circle them, and mark them with the number 2, the houses from which you told us that you saw fire coming from.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: These are these houses here, which I just circled and marked with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the area where the mortar grenades fell?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is this area, here. This is where the mortars fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark this area with the number 3.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you saw that there was fire from the houses which you marked, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: At that moment, we were just observing. We did not undertake any activities towards these positions, up until the moment when from point 2 and from other points, there was incoming fire towards us, towards the position of Smok. At that time, I called Major Mitre Despodov and I informed him of the situation. I told him that our point was under attack, and he told me to discover the targets and to act on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the markings seem to have been lost on the picture. Therefore, it seems we would have to do this again, that we would have to go through the marking procedure again. At least I don't see these markings on the screen in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It appear it will need to be repeated. Oh, all is saved, thankfully. You wish to tender them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they're preserved as we had them marked, that I would first propose that this be put on the 65 ter list and then that it be received in evidence. Oh, yes, I see them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The photograph as marked will become an exhibit and the photograph will be added to the list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit 2D87, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, could you please continue telling us what you did after you spoke with your superior, Major Despodov?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Once I spoke to him and once he approved action, first, I ordered the soldiers who were at the Smok position to use machine-guns and the sniper that was positioned at the Smok position, to open fire towards the persons who were shooting towards us. Also, to my units, the mortars, I gave them elements to open fire towards this position, the point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did they do so?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we did so. We fired the mortars and the soldiers also used the machine-guns and the sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At that period of time, in this area which we're looking at the screen right now, did you notice down there, members of the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: At that moment we did not notice such members of the security forces. Much later we noticed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When did you notice them for the first time in this area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say after 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the photograph once again, please. Could we -- could the witness please be shown once again Exhibit 2D87.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where you noticed the Macedonian security forces in the village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We noticed them later, in the area of this house, in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could ask the court usher to assist the witness to mark these with the colour blue.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: In this area, we noticed them in this area for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did they fire towards the position which you marked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, they were firing towards point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please put the number 4 next to the area which you just marked in blue.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How long did this last? How long did this firing last?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say that it lasted quite some time, over an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Until when did you fire with the mortars and the infantry weapons from the Smok position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We fired up until we noticed the security forces. When we noticed them, we stopped firing towards that target, because there was danger that we might hit them. Then we continued to fire towards the other targets that we had discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this photograph in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D88, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said earlier that there was fire towards you from other positions as well.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There was such fire from other positions, two other positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what those positions were?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This was target number 2, an old house, where I think they were shooting with snipers. There was a balcony and there was a kneeling person on that balcony firing. From the third place, a house, looking towards Rastanski Pat, at the end of the village of Ljuboten from the roof there was machine gun-fire coming towards us.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You now told us that you think that there was sniper fire coming from point 2. How did you come about this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I concluded this because the person was moving the weapons towards us and his gun-fire came to our positions. If this had been an ordinary gun this would not have been possible because this was a distance of about 400 metres, and it is difficult for an automatic gun to reach this distance. Also, the same person was aiming his shots towards the police. At one moment he was shooting towards us and at one moment towards the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see an optical aim from -- on this gun?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: From this position, we were not able to see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown photograph 65 ter 178, N003-0371.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this photo taken from the position of Smok?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark the place that you talked about previously, which is the place that you located as a target, and if you can encircle it.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you explain what kind of terrain is that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: From our position we could see that that was a densely populated area with lots of houses, and they were looking at the valley of the village. So, here, down below, there is a valley and a road that leads to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If, looking from the position that you encircled, there is a road, what is that road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That is the road that leads from the valley and goes to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark that road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please put number 1 next to the circle; and number 2 next to the road.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From the position that you marked with number 1, is that position on the same level with the road looking at the -- towards the church?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is on the same level with the houses that are next to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Between the church and the point 1, is the road on the same level?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. The road goes downhill towards the valley and then it goes up to the point 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So if a person is in the valley, that person would be on a lower level than the point 1?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That means that the person would have to go up, uphill.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have any activities against this target?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We used the mortars, the machine-guns, and the sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this photograph as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 2D89, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The photograph that you were explaining just now, first, did you notice members of Macedonian security forces in the course of that Sunday?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: You mean near point 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: For the first time we noticed them around 10.00, maybe even later.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was it exactly near point 1?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Because that is where we had a good site. We couldn't really see what was happening in the valley, but we could see when people were coming uphill.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Near point 1, did you see the advances of the security forces?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say that their advancing was very slow. Actually, they couldn't advance at all because they were a target of a fire attack until the APCs arrived, which helped them at that time. The APC was protecting the soldiers because it was moving ahead and the soldiers were following the transporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said when you were on the position of Smok, you located a third place as an enemy attack fire.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which part was that? What part of the village was that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Those were the houses on Rastanski Pat where the village of Ljuboten ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am aware of the time and I would like to continue with questions about the next position, so maybe if this is the right time to have a break and then I continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. We will have the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 178, N003-0368.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photo?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me where was this picture taken from; can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was taken from the position of Smok.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the road to Rastak?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on this photograph the place from where your positions were fired at?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I see the position where the fire was opened at our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the road to Rastak?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you put number 1.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the position or the place from where shots were fired on that Sunday morning against the position of Smok.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. From this place shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was this the only place from where shots fired that morning?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. The first houses from these four houses that was early in the morning when the fire started, and then the machine-gun moved to this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the previous house with number 2.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And then mark the houses where the fire started. Could you put number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How did you notice that shots were fired at you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: From the roof of the house, the roof tiles were removed, and we saw a machine-gun. The machine-gun had a whole barrage of shot that could be heard from our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which house are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: House number 2, point number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How metres [as interpreted] was this house away from your position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Around 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The place that you marked with number 3, could you tell me how did you see the fires and where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: First, the fires were shot from the balconies, and then the fire stopped and moved to point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You mean point 2, marked on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask that this photograph is put on the 65 ter list and is accepted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. Apostolski, would you be able to clarify with the witness the fire that he described coming from house number 3 are earlier in the morning, what type of weapon or weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, when you saw the firing from the position marked with number 3, what kind of weapon was used?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: With machine-gun, because it was a long-lasting barrage of shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How many weapons did you see in that position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We suspected there were two weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How many did you see?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: On the house marked with number 1, we personally saw the weapon; and on the -- from the house number 3, we heard a pair of weapons, so we suspected that there was another house next to house number 3 where shots were fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you think that those fires were coming from a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: One could have been an automatic gun, but it was a burst of fire, so we suspect that if one opens fire from that distance against the security forces near the church, it could have been a machine-gun, because an automatic rifle doesn't have that range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt I'm just hoping for some clarification. On the transcript at line 11 refers to weapons being seen on the house marked with number 1. There is no house marked with number 1 in the picture. So I was just hoping that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me, which house you had in mind, because on the transcript it is said house marked with number 1 where you saw the shots being fired from.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We saw the first shots from the houses marked with 3 and then the shots moved from the house marked with number 2. It was some time after 9.00 when the shots were fired from the house number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where did you see the weapons?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The houses that are marked with number 3, the weapons were on the balconies, while the house marked with number 2 the roof tiles were removed and the shots were fired from the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was the shooter on the roof of the house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, from the inside of the roof. The roof tiles were just removed and the shots were fired from that spot. We couldn't see the body of the person. We could only see the flame of the machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this photograph be accepted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D90, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you fire towards these positions, towards this position that I just asked you about on Sunday in the morning?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We did fire towards the house marked --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness has his microphone off. Could you please ask him to turn it on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were firing towards the house marked with number 2 with the mortars. We fired with a 120-millimetre mortars. We also fired towards that position with a sniper and with a machine-gun, and then towards the point 3 we only fire in the morning with a machine-gun and with a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your explanation. You previously testified that it has been fired from several positions in the morning on Sunday, on 12th of August. In the course of the day, as the day went on, was it fired from other weapons towards your position of Smok?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. After 11.00, fire was opened towards our position, also from the position of Bel Kamen with an 82-millimetre mortars. The shells were falling at the position of Smok, Bomba, and at the mortar battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What did you do when they started to fire on your positions with the mortars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I ordered my soldiers to take shelter and I ordered -- I gave elements to the mortar battery and ordered it to open fire towards the Bel Kamen position which it did. My battery fired a number of shells towards that region and then the firing stopped later.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the other mortars within your -- did other mortars or other weapons fire towards their positions?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We fired with the 82-millimetre mortars towards their position. They were the one firing, but they were under the command of another officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Under which command were those mortars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Under the command of Lieutenant Brasnarski Darko.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Once the firing stopped towards your position with the mortars, and after you returned by firing with the mortars, in the village of Ljuboten, did you notice any Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The security forces were already deeper in the village. They were somewhere after the mosque towards the -- at the road towards Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me how were they making progress at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: They were going rather slowly. The APC went in front of them and it was followed by the police officers and they went rather slowly. It was fired against them from the house number 2 that was on the picture before.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, at the previous picture, the house numbered with number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where was it fired at from that house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Towards the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What did you see after that? What happened later? Did the APC stop there? Did it go -- did it continue?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The APC, sometime around 12.00, came to the house marked with number 3, and then the fire stopped, both -- both from the terrorists and the fires also stopped from the security forces. At that moment, out of the house marked with number 2, there was an a haystack behind it and we saw terrorists running towards the forest. That was a group of five or around five terrorists that were running towards the forest and carrying weapons with them. I ordered my soldiers to open fire with snipers and machine-guns and rifles, but what was important was the fire with the machine-gun and sniper. We surely hit one person at that time and two or three of them ran -- managed to escape towards the village, towards the forest. And once the police saw that we were firing against the terrorists as they were in the proximity around the houses -- around the house number 3, they took positions around the house number 2 and started firing towards them, towards the person that were trying to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me go a step back now. You said you saw -- you said that you hit one person from your positions. Could you describe how did you know -- how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm sure about one because a sniper that fired first hit the person. That was the only weapon firing at that time and that person fell down. That's why I'm sure we hit one person and once the other soldiers started firing, as well as the police, then big noise took place from the firing and I saw them running away. I saw two or three persons running away, and I don't know what happened with the other persons that got out of the house. I didn't see whether they fell down or escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the persons that you didn't see. Maybe they were hit by the firings from your position? Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say that the soldiers that were around me were saying that they hit them, but I didn't see them personally. They were commenting that they have hit two more persons, but I didn't saw them -- I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At that time the soldiers that were firing from the Smok position, were they all members of your battery?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: There were only four soldiers in my battery while the other soldiers were from the 1st Infantry Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At that moment who was in command, who was the head of the position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I was in command for them as well, because when an officer is there, all the soldiers are under his command, regardless of the fact that they are on the other position, so the highest ranking officer is the one who is in command at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And after that stop -- when did the shooting stop towards those persons?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The shooting started -- stopped soon after that because there were no targets anymore, there were no terrorists. The police already reached the end of the village and there was no shooting. I remained one more hour at my position to analyse the situation and since it was peaceful there was no shooting anymore, I withdrew with my soldiers to the children's rest house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let us go a step back. At -- towards what direction were they running away?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm very sorry to interrupt. I just need to point out that this testimony on a crucial issue in this case is something which we haven't received any notice of. There are suspect interviews of witness in which this matter has never been mentioned. The notice we were given of witness's testimony also fails to mention anything about sniper shooting from the position and actually hitting these particular individuals. This may be something which is going to have some impact on -- obviously on our cross-examination and the time any further time we may need to prepare for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment that is noted, Mr. Dobbyn. And we will see how the matter emerges when you do cross-examine, whether you have need for some further delay. Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has testified about these matters in the interview that he given before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's no need to debate that now, Mr. Apostolski. Carry on with your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. I thank you. Could the witness be shown Exhibit 1D128, please. No, this is not the document. I might have misspoken. Could it be shown 2D31, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Before you are shown, I'd like to ask you whether you wrote some written reports regarding these events.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I wrote a statement, a report to the commander, Mitre Despodov, right after the events of 13th -- on 13th or 14th of August I was asked to write a report about the firing towards the village, towards what targets, and the report referred to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 2D31, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on the screen in front of you a report?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is my report that I wrote for the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You personally wrote this one?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'll read it now. This is a report on command and combat activities on 12th of August, 2001. "On 12th of August, 2001, in the morning I was at the rest house carrying out my regular duties, and at around 8.00 we heard several long bursts of fire which kept repeating. Then I received a call from the battalion commander, who ordered me to occupy the observation post in the sector of the Smok sector and to prepare the battery for action. "After I carry out the necessary preparations, four of my soldiers occupied the observation post at about 8.30. At that moment the combat was still going on. Having observed the village I established that the terrorists were opening fire from the sector around the church. Most probably there was a sniper fire in an old house at about ten metres below the mosque, and machine-gun fire was coming from the area above the mosque, from the four houses and the machine-gun was fired towards us. "I then informed the commander about the situation, and he ordered me to destroy the targets with several 120-millimetre mortar shells. In the time between 9.00 and 10.00 hours, we fired several shells, and we fired around eight around the church. We fired five shells at the sniper and I fired three shells at the machine-gun. During the combat activities in the village of Ljuboten, I fired a total of 600 120-millimetre shells. The combat activities continued, but as the police entered the village after 10.00, I carried out no activities with my battery in the Ljuboten village." Is this the report that you have written?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It has been written immediately after the events and this is -- it reflects the picture that you have seen on 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As you said, this has been written on the 13th of August, and represents the real picture of that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a little bit more about this report. What did Major Despodov tell you, how to write your report?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: To write a report about where we fired at in the village, to describe the targets. That was it. And that's why this is a brief report, just explaining the targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When I read this to you at one place you say, "Above the mosque in the four houses, in two of them in the four new houses there was a machine-gun firing at us." What houses did have you in mind in this report?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Those were the houses that were marked with the number 3 on the previous photograph. When I telephoned the major in the morning, when I informed him that we are fired at, those were the houses that the fire was coming from, the house marked with number 3. That's why we wrote this. We informed the major what are the exact houses that the fire is coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the major ask you to inform him about the number of mines that you -- the shells that you have fired?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I was supposed to write that in my report, and I wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you ask me -- could you tell me specifically about what part and what shells are mentioned in the report?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: These are only about the village of Ljuboten. The targets in the village of Ljuboten. The targets 1, 2, and 3. To write a report about these targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you said that you also fired towards Bel Kamen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, this is not mentioned in this report because the major asked us only to describe the firing that we had towards the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the Exhibit P306, please. Could we please see the second page of the Macedonian version, please. The English can remain as is. Could we please scroll up a little bit so we can see the lower -- the lower part of the document. A little more, please. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see a signature at the bottom of this page?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As can I see here, it says Lieutenant Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Lieutenant Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He was the commander of the 1st Infantry Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you speaking of him when you were saying that he had under his command mortars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Lieutenant Mario Jurisic was the commander of the 1st company and within his company there was a platoon -- mortar platoon and a cannon platoon, 176-millimetre and the commander of the mortar cannon was the Brasnarski, Darko. This platoon was within the unit of Mario.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can we now look at the first page of the document, please. Do you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is information from Lieutenant Mario Jurisic regarding the combat activities on the 12th of August, 2001. Here it reads: "At 8.00 on 12th of August 2001, one could hear shots in the area of Ljuboten village. The right wing of the defence of the company informed us through a wire connection that they had come under attack by machine-gun and sniper fire at the observation Smok." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there members of the company of Mario Jurisic at the Smok position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, they were constantly on duty there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there wire link between him and the position of his mortar?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. All positions had a wire link with the rest house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
