utterances.text: Then it says: "I immediately informed the commander of the battalion who ordered me and my deputy to climb up to the position and to observe the situation. "I climbed to the point under attack whereas my deputy went a bit towards the north at the position of B1 and was ordered to be prepared for action in case of need. I start immediately with locating targets and actions from infantry weapons towards strictly selected targets, exclusively from the far lower point, reinforced with five soldiers. All other check-points were in readiness for action because of the possibility of attack from other directions. "After 9.00, my deputy informed me that his positions at B1 had come under sniper and machine-gun fire. From the old house, near the mosque with sniper, and from the last new houses close to the road, the second one of the four possible ones, there was fire on our position by machine-gun. After approval from the commander of the battalion, I received an order to support this activity by cannons against the confirmed targets until they were eliminated. After the activations of the cannons, we started to regroup, the DTG began to regroup." Can you tell us what this means "DT" means?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is diversion terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "And started to move towards the village and at the same time continued to shoot against our positions. I immediately requested approval from the commander of the battalion to use the 82-millimetre mortars, and after the approval, I fired five projectiles, 82-millimetres, against the DTG at the front part of the houses. The police had already entered the village so we stopped the activities. "At about 11.00, our positions came under fire of 82-millimetre mortars, and during this time the shells were falling on our positions. We established that the fire was coming from the small forest near the village. Upon an order, the deputy fired five projectiles from the observation post over the positions of the DTG." Can you tell us what this means?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This means the firing position of the diversion and terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "After the fifth grenade the fire stopped. Later our activities in Ljuboten village stopped. The police undertook further activities." Does this information, regarding the combat activities on the 12th of August, 2001, are identical with your understanding of the events?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have the description of the activities in the village from the positions of Lieutenant Jurisic, from his viewpoint, but they correspond to the situation in the village at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 1D281.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see it clearly?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. If it could be enlarged, it would be a better -- better view.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please enlarge this photograph in the right corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photograph which the Prosecution showed me during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we can't see the picture very clearly, can we please see 1D281.3. I think this is a clearer photograph. Yes, this is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the same photograph as the one you saw previously?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see it more clearly now?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when speaking with the Prosecution, you said you had two conversations. Did you mark anything? Did they show you any photographs which you marked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I did mark this photograph. This marking is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please clarify, I see here that Smok is written.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And a line next to it. What is it that you were marking?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: At this moment I can say that the position Smok is not marked very precisely. I think I have missed the distance. It's a little bit-- a bit further down towards the rocks?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this photograph was taken from?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Probably from the position of Mecka, much higher up.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You have noted here "church," "crkva"?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is it that you have marked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: R-4, "crkva."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this means?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This means "reper," benchmark 4, this is the markings we use which I explained earlier, markings, benchmarks which we place before we begin any combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this marks the church?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Then we see C-1. You have markings of three to four terrorists.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is target 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are these the same houses which you marked previously?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. These are the same houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please shift the photograph towards the left. This would be 1D281, 1D281.2. Please move the picture up a little bit. Could we please scroll up some more to see what the markings are.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I see here that you have marked C-2, sniper?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: C-2, sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What did you mean by this marking?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is C-2, target 2, the houses were from where the sniper was firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And this is circled in white?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And underneath it says 628.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I recall now, I think this was the number of mines when I was asked by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Then I see the marking R-2, mosque.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is benchmark 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please scroll on further to the left. We will not be able to see this on this photograph. Could we please open D281.1 -- 1D281.1. If we could enlarge this picture somewhat. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Here we have machine-gun written.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you have circled one house.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is target 3, the house from where the machine-gun was firing from.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what R-1, Grobista marks?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is the benchmark, the aiming mark 1, the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the house which is marked with the machine-gun, is this the same house which you marked earlier?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Now can I see that it is not the same house. This picture is taken from a different position. At that time I was led to mark the house I did mark because it seemed closer to the positions of Smok. Also, there's a haystack behind this house while at the moment when there were combat activities, the house which I marked previously with the number 2, had a haystack and from there, the terrorists were fleeing. The nylon over the haystack led me to think that this was the house in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So let us clear this up. This photograph that the Prosecution showed you, does it correspond, is it taken from your position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. I presume it was taken from the position of Mecka or Volk.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness, again, please be shown 2D90, Exhibit 2D90.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please clarify what you were saying earlier?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. On this picture we can see the house which I have marked as a target, number 3, and this house is located right in front of point 2. When I can see from this angle -- from the angle of the Smok position, I'm sure that this was the house from where fires came from point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court usher please assist the witness to circle this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark this with the number 4. And for the purpose of the transcript, this is the house which the witness says the witness marked on Exhibit 1D281 as point 3.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, could you please mark the haystack which you were describing as the place from where the terrorists were fleeing in 2001? Could you mark it where it was? Line 18, can you -- for the purpose of the transcript can you please mark the haystack. Haystack.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me what a haystack is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: A haystack is a place covered with the nylon where tobacco is kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is the purpose of this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This nylon is placed there to keep things from getting wet or if vegetables are in question to make them ripe [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark where this was?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This was right behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark this with the number 5 in blue.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see such a nylon covering near the house marked with number 4?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: From this angle I cannot say, but from the previous picture I could see that there was such a nylon covering near the point 4, the house marked with number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let us clarify once again. Let us go back to Exhibit 1D281.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, we seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can the Chamber be clear what is intended by the evidence, Mr. Apostolski. Is the witness saying that the area now marked with a blue 4 is the position previously marked by the witness but wrongly marked by the witness, he then thinking it was the house which he now sees is house marked 2 in red.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have different understandings of the effect of the evidence. I've given you one, if the witness is able to confirm that, fine; but if not, you might need to explore further with the witness. Because we really have been somewhat confused by this passage of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with this picture, I wanted to explain the difference in markings in 1D281, the previous panoramic picture, which we saw which the witness marked when speaking with the investigators, and what is being marked now with number 2. Now number 4 marks that which the witness had marked on the Exhibit 1D281 as the position of the machine-gun, but since he was not at the position as the picture from the Prosecution, I wanted to show him a photograph from the position where he was located in order that he be able to clarify this and to make it more clear. Therefore, the correct house on this picture where the machine-gun was located is the house marked with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D91, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit P303.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the Official Note in the upper left corner? It says, "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Defence, the army General Staff," and below it says, "The 1st Guardist Brigade, Captain First Class Ljupco Kostadinov." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Ljupco Kostadinov?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes he was a security organ in the 1st Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the page 2, opened, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you see in front of you the paragraph 3 that starts with the word: "On Sunday, 12th of August ..."

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, in this photograph it is said that: "On Sunday, 12 August 2001 at 4.30, the person Johan Tarculovski with other persons (reservists of the Ministry of Interior) started the action. Immediately after the start of the action, Captain Nikolce Grozdanovski, called Major Despodov and informed him about the start of the action that was organised by the Ministry of Interior. "The reservists, wearing MOI uniforms, advanced towards the village up to the point on the bridge where there was a check-point and the house of the person Kenan. When they saw that they couldn't advance anymore they called Major Despodov and they requested support because the buildings were defended by machine-guns. After the agreement with Major Despodov, the persons withdrew to a safe place and the first grenades were fired at 5.30 at the mentioned building. "When they opened fire at the mentioned buildings from the village of Ljubanci towards the position of the 3rd Guardist Brigade, armed terrorists started to flee whereby fire was opened from the cannon B-1, 76-millimetres and the anti-aircraft cannons of the 3rd Guardist Brigade." How would you comment on this one?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, sir, this is not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which part is not true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: First the description of the event is not true, nor it is the time that is put here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this document that states that the first grenades were fired at 5.30, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit P304.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the upper left corner, you can see the head line Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Defence, the army General Staff, 1st Guardist Brigade. This is a report about the area of the 3rd Guardist Brigade and this is sent to General Major Sokol Mitrevski. Could we now see the last page. Do you see the last page?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You see signed by Colonel Blazo Kopacev. Do you know Colonel Blazo Kopacev?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, he was the commander of the 1st Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we go back to the first page of the document, please. The second page of the document, if possible. Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see in the beginning of the document that reads "On the 12th of August at 4.30 the action started and around 5.30 to 6.00 the first mortar from the mortar of 120-millimetre was fired upon request of Mr. Johan because he found fire spots which he requested to be neutralized."

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "The commander of the 3rd Guardist Brigade satisfied this request and began firing 120-millimetre mortar." How would you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say that this is completely untrue.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me if a shell is fired at 5.30 in the morning and if it lands in the village of Ljuboten, 5.30 a.m. is a quiet part of the day. Where would that shell be heard?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: It would probably have been heard all the way to Skopje, because 5.30 is peaceful part of the day and the sound could have been heard all the way to the city of Skopje, because it is an open area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your answer. Could you now focus a little further on the list, on the paragraph that starts with the words: "On the 12th of August 2001 in his regular morning report at 0640, Major Mitre Despodov informed that there had been no problems that night except that soldiers who were guarding the Belgian camp had fired three or four bursts of fire out of fear." Now, reading this paragraph I would continue about the same day. "He phoned me again at 8.30 hours and asked me to check whether General Sokol Mitrevski had any information about the operations in the Ljuboten village." If shells were fired at 5.30 in the morning, would they be heard in the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. And I find it really strange that Major Kopacev didn't hear them or anybody else if there was an action that early in the morning. I'm sure that some of his colleagues or the police or anybody in the General Staff would have heard it, and I find it really strange that nobody knew about this up to 8.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. What I just read on the 12th of August 2001 Major Mitre Despodov informed me that there had been no problems in the area that evening, does that correspond to the truth?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: When he was reporting at 6.40 that there had been no problems in the area of his battalion proves that up to 6.40 in the morning there had been no combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Residovic, do you have any examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just have several questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Grozdanovski. I am Edina Residovic and together with Mr. Mettraux we are defending Mr. Boskoski. During the hearing you told my colleague Apostolski that on the 10th of August, when you went to see the spot where the mine was planted by NLA, that you were called by your superiors. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that there were called by the commander of the first guard battalion, Kopacev and the commander of the defence of the city of Skopje, General Sokol Mitrevski. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that the General Sokol Mitrevski requested from you to inform him about the situation and he gave you some orders. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Grozdanovski, did you obey those orders that were given to you by General Mitrevski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We carry out the orders, we opened fire towards the terrorists to expel them from the place where we were. They -- they had to be distanced in order for the transport helicopter to be able to land and take the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Explaining who your immediate superior was, you said that was commander of the battalion, Major Mitre Despodov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But being a soldier and officer, you had the obligation to obey the orders of a higher superior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. In our command system, if we receive a command for a higher superior we are obliged to carry out this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have to obey that order whether it is oral or written order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment even a verbal order was sufficient for us to carry it out. The situation imposed this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you agree with me, Mr. Grozdanovski, that if such an order had been issued by the supreme commander you being an officer would have had the obligation to obey that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, certainly of the when the supreme commander would have issued an order then we would of course have carried out his order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Grozdanovski, you were the commander of the mortar battery. Let us suppose one situation. If in the course of any operation, any combat operation, you were given a person that was not a soldier or if you had a soldier from another army unit or a police officer from a police station or an army reservist, or a police reservist, who would be the commander of these persons?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: When other persons are joined to the army, in the case that they're not members of the army, they're put under our command. We command with them. If it is a military person that is added and of a higher rank, then this person takes the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what I understood from what you were saying is that irrespective of the status of the person who is not a soldier but is put in a combat situation to work jointly with the army, then the army commander is also commander to these persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, you said that very often you were visiting the position of Smok before the events that took place -- between the 10th and 12th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And from that position, you could very well observe the village of Ljuboten, just as we saw on several photographs that were shown to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that from the soldiers and from other persons you had information about movement during the night or movements of weapons and similar. I wouldn't like to repeat everything that you said. Please, tell me, you also said that personally you did not see any activities in the village, any fortification activities. Do you remember saying that to my learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I recall. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, do you know or are you familiar with the method of building houses in a traditional Albanian village, just as Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I know this. The houses have high walls around the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If a person walks down the street between these houses, is that person able to see what is going on behind those walls?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. The person is not able to see anything because these are two metre high walls or higher. One cannot see what is going on beyond the walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me, Mr. Grozdanovski, that these walls around the houses in the village of Ljuboten were practically a natural fortification for possible attacks from the house yards or the houses themselves? Could you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is absolutely correct. There was one such example where terrorists were shooting from the wall. They used the wall and they shot from this wall towards the security forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you are an artillery person and you were a commander of mortar batteries -- no, let me ask you something else before that. Having in mind the position that you held at the time, tell me, is it correct that the houses in the village of Ljuboten very frequently were built in a row and they were connected with these high walls?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The houses were very densely positioned, one next to another. In many places, they were built in this fashion. They were very densely located.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since this is a village not far away from Skopje, please tell me, if you know at all, what was this population mainly occupied with?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I was able to see from the period I was there, mainly they occupied themselves with agriculture and cattle herding. They had shepherd.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, in addition to the houses where the Ljuboten villagers lived, were there any other buildings that were related to their agricultural activities that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. They usually have facilities where they kept hay and cattle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From those positions, could you see whether there were any tractors or oil tanks in the house yards? Were there any vehicles? Do you know if it was customary to have any kind of equipment in the house yards in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Most of the houses did have tractors. We could see them moving during the day so there were plenty of tractors in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now being an artillery person and you're a major, you must know the consequences or the effects of one mortar shell. Could you please tell me, a mortar shell, can it, if at all, cause fire?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: A mortar shell has the purpose to destroy and to kill. There is a possibility to set a facility on fire or to cause similar effects in a situation when there are easily inflammable substances such as gas, oil, hay, in such cases it may occur that a fire is caused.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, a mortar shell, if it hits the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Defence counsel has her microphone switched off. Could we ask the Defence counsel to repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, if I understood you well, if a mortar shell hits an inflammable substance - as you said, oil, gas, hay - it can cause fire?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. When we go to train in Krivolak, it often happens that we set on fire dry hay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said there was a higher number of reservists in your battery. Could you tell me whether the company of Commander Jurisic, they were also reservists?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The company of Jurisic Mario, the whole 3rd Guardist Battalion was composed of reservists. As far as I recall there was only one regular soldier. He was a driver. Just one. All other soldiers were reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me whether some of the reservists were coming from the surrounding villages, especially the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. A large number of them were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Replying to the questions of my learned colleague, you said that after the killing of the soldiers in the mine blast some of the soldiers had a very low morale. Could you tell me, since we are talking about reservists and persons that were hurt by this tragedy that happened to the army of the Republic of Macedonia, do you exclude the possibility that some soldiers could have opened fire, sporadic fire, against the village without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say that it is possible. However, as for my battery, I can say that there was no fire from the 120-millimetre mortars on the village because we always had an officer at the positions and in no one moment did he inform me that the village was fired upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And one last question, Mr. Grozdanovski. Having in mind the vicinity of the position of Smok, was there a possibility that some of the army could have entered the village that morning?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: On the 12th, up until 2.00, around 2.00, while I was at the position, no soldier left in the direction towards the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Grozdanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. I think the time suggests this would be a practical moment to have the second break. We will do so and resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Grozdanovski. My name is Gerard Dobbyn. I'm representing the Office of the Prosecutor today, and following on from the questions that my learned colleagues have asked you I'm going to be spending some time asking you some more questions about the events that you've described. Now, you've described how you were interviewed as a suspect by the Office of the Prosecutor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And there were two separate interview, isn't that right, one was on the 30th of July, 2004 and the other one was on the 8th of November, 2004?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you have an interpreter present during both of these interviews?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, there was an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall being advised of certain rights that you had as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I was advised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And among the rights that you were advised of, do you recall being advised that you had the right not to answer any questions?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall being advised that you also had the right to have a lawyer present during the interviews?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And also isn't that right that you were advised that at the end of each interview you would be given an opportunity to give any additional information that you wanted to and also to clarify any points that had come up during the interviews?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, finally, do you recall being advised that these interviews would be recorded?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, during these two interviews, did you attempt to answer all of the questions put to you truthfully and as fully as possible?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you attempt to mislead the interviewers at any time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no, I did not attempt to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you deliberately hide any facts from the interviewers during these interviews?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I have not hidden anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. So it would be fair to say that during these interviews you were -- you tried to be honest throughout them and provide a full picture of the events?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I tried to be as honest as I could, as truthful as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like just to move on and perhaps ask you some of the question just clarifying further some of the points you've covered earlier about the army positions around Ljuboten. And, again, just to be clear, I believe you testified that during the events in Ljuboten in 2001, you were the captain of the 120-millimetre Mortar Battery of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is it correct also that you were posted in the Ljubanci-Ljuboten area from the 12th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So by the time the events of the weekend of the 10th to 12th August occurred, you had been there for approximately two months?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I believe you also described that the headquarters of the 3rd Battalion was in the school in Ljubanci. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And your unit, the mortar battery, was housed in the children's rest house above Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And also housed there was the company that was commanded by Mario Jurisic. Is that also right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you just remind me again, what -- what company was that, that Mario Jurisic commanded?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And that was an infantry company?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, infantry company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And your mortar battery consisted of 120-millimetre mortars, correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the 2nd Company -- sorry, the 1st Company, Mario Jurisic's company, that had also had 82-millimetre mortars; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Grozdanovski --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And Your Honours, we have prepared some binders for this witness and I would ask that they be distributed at this time. Now, if we could show 65 ter 1231.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Grozdanovski, this is in tab 5 of the binder in front of you. So if you could turn to tab 5, please. And what you have in front of you, Mr. Grozdanovski, is a map showing police, army, and NLA positions in the Ljubanci-Ljuboten area in August 2001. Do you recall seeing this map before, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in fact you were shown this map, weren't you, during your suspect interview on the 30th of July, 2004?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you look at the top left-hand corner this is written in English. I'll read it to you. It says, "Attachment Suspect Interview, Grozdanovski Nikolce" -- sorry, I'll try your name again. "Grozdanovski Nikolce, 30 July 2004, Skopje field office, Investigator Kuehnel," and then it has a signature underneath that. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you look at the bottom of the page, is that your signature there, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you accept, don't you, that this picture accurately reflects the positions that your army unit had around the village of Ljuboten at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, where on this map exactly were your mortars positioned?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: My mortar positions are marked with "Zvero."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Actually, that's fine. I think it's already marked on the map. So we have the confirmation, but thank you for your assistance. And from Svero was it possible to see into Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you testified earlier on that you had two observation posts, one at Smok, and one at place called Zdravec. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you look at the bottom of the map you'll see handwriting, "Zdravec," with a line going up to a position just to the left of the red explosion, did you put that in there yourself, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this represents the position of your observation post at Zdravec?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I believe you stated earlier that the observation post -- sorry, your observation post at Smok was inactive. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could you please explain a bit more fully what you mean by it being inactive?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: At the position Smok, my battery had a wire link from Smok to my battery, which was there and in the case of need that we be able to establish immediate contact with my subordinate, Slavco Butilovski. We had no soldiers -- there were no soldiers, my soldiers who were on duty all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. What optical equipment did you have at Zdravec?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: At Zdravec, my soldiers had artillery compass and binoculars, while the soldiers from the infantry of Mario's unit had night visions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can you explain what an artillery compass is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: They have an optical device on them. They have a compass, there's a compass, and they serve to establish the angle to the target, and then this angle is used while we're firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this artillery compass, does it also magnify?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I said this. There is an optical device in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what level of magnification are these capable of achieving?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Sixfold magnifying power.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what about the binoculars that you had? What level of magnification do they have?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We had binoculars with sixfold and eightfold magnifying power.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did you also have similar equipment available to you when you were at Smok observation post?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The same binoculars and the same artillery compass.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, is it possible, Mr. Grozdanovski, to see Ljuboten village from the Zdravec observation post?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes it is possible, from the position of Zdravec one could see the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And obviously the village is also visible from Smok and Bomba, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. It is -- it was best visible from the Smok position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now if you look to the bottom left of this map, you'll see a scale there, Mr. Grozdanovski. Do you see that? Sorry, to the bottom left of your map.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And using this scale as a reference, would you agree that the distance from Smok -- actually, if I just take a step back. In the village of Ljuboten, can you also see symbols for the orthodox church and the mosque?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And using the scale at the bottom left as a reference would you agree that the distance from Smok to the orthodox church is somewhere between one to two kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, about one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, again the distance from Smok to the mosque would also be somewhere between one and two kilometres. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would you agree that the distance from Smok to the northeastern edge of Ljuboten village to the right of the mosque as it appears here, would be closer to two kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe it's less. About a kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, looking from the scale that we have at the bottom of the map wouldn't you agree that, according to that, it would be closer to two kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: We can estimate, but perhaps we should measure it more precisely to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'll move on from there. Do you see also the map indicates the location of the mine incident at Ljubotenski Bacila, doesn't it? And that's shown by a red explosion symbol.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, again, referring to the scale on the map, would you agree that this shows the distance from Ljubotenski Bacila to Ljuboten would be somewhere in the range of perhaps seven to eight kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As an estimate, I can agree, but it would be better if we were to measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, regardless of the distance that it shows in a straight line from Ljubotenski Bacila to Ljuboten, in fact, it takes -- it would be a much further distance than a straight-line distance wouldn't it to actually get there because the roads are not straight but wind around the mountains and valley. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I'd like it tender 65 ter 1231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P595, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I would ask that now we show ERN number N005-7603, and this is a photograph that is taken from page 5 of the Prosecution's Court binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, do you see the photograph in front of you, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would you agree that this is a panoramic photograph taken from the south-east of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, in this photograph, are any of the locations where the army units were positioned in August 2001 visible?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have the usher's assistance at this time. And if perhaps with circles you could mark any locations where the army was positioned during August 2001.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. I see that you've marked three circles and also an arrow. Let's start from the left. The circle on the left, what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The Smok position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you please put the number 1 underneath that.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the second circle, to the right of that, what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The Mecka position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you put a number 2 by that, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you go to the far right, what is the third circle?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Number 2 was position Bomba, and the third circle is the Mecka position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. So just for the record, if we'll make that clear the circle with the number 2 represents Bomba. Correct? And if --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, Bomba.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could put a number 3 by the third circle representing Mecka.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is the Mecka position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And I see these, what I take to be an arrow, above the 1st circle labeled number 1; what does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The arrow is behind the hill, behind this in the valley behind this arrow was the mortar battery, behind the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If you could put a number 4 above that arrow then. Thank you, Mr. Grozdanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this photograph at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P596, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Grozdanovski, I would just like to clarify perhaps through a few questions the composition of your mortar battery. Now, I believe you stated that you had six 120-millimetre mortars in your battery. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And how many soldiers manned each individual mortar?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As a rule, five soldiers and one commander should be manning a mortar. But in no moment did we have a sufficient number. We had four or three, depending on the month and the coming of the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And apart from the people manning the mortars, did you have any other members of your units?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There was a command platoon that included the liaison officers, the scouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And earlier in your testimony you made reference to snipers. Were snipers part of your mortar battery?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, the snipers were members of the 1st Infantry Brigade who were at the Smok position, who were at that position. They were from the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So they were under the command of Mario Jurisic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, in their everyday activities they were under the command of Lieutenant Mario Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at Smok -- [Microphone not activated] Sorry, I'll ask that again. At the Smok position were they located in exactly the same area that you were?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We were at the same shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you described a trench that runs along the Smok position where you could kneel in without being visible. Were your positions in front of or behind those trenches?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The Smok position composed of two parts: The point marked with the number 1 is the observation post; while in the area now marked with the number 4 was the bunker from Smok. These two parts were connected by a trench, a dug in trench. The bunker was used for the soldiers who were on duty be able to rest. The soldiers on duty observed from point 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did they observe from within the trench?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: It was also possible to observe from the trench. It was about one half metre so that a person was able to kneel without -- and move without being seen. However, one could also observe from there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, the snipers that were connected with Mario Jurisic's unit, do you know what fire-arms they had, what weapons they had?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: They had a 7.9-millimetre sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And how many snipers were there in that unit?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Each unit that was on duty had one sniperist. Let's say Mario's group of five people had one sniper and efforts were made for each position to have one sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So just to be clear from that are you saying that on the 12th of August from Smok there would have been just one sniperist there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe that there were two, because, at that moment, the unit which is not on duty, was at the position Smok. Therefore, the unit which, under normal conditions would have been resting at the rest house, was then at the position. This is speaking about the soldiers of Mario Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, just one minute, Mr. Grozdanovski. Now, in response to questions from my learned colleague earlier on, you described a certain actions taking place around Ljuboten, leading up to the events of 10th to 12th of August, which you took, you described as being indicative of NLA activity around Ljuboten. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You described movement around certain areas, people moving into Ljuboten, other indications such as ammunition being found on the road. Do you recall describing that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'd like to go into that just a little bit further and ask specifically about your personal knowledge of the situation around Ljuboten, leading up to the 10th to 12th of August. And isn't it true, Mr. Grozdanovski, that from your point of view in the two months prior to the events in Ljuboten the general security situation in the Ljuboten area was good?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Generally speaking it was good. Because there was no combat action.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And isn't it true that you didn't have -- your unit, the army units around that area didn't have any problems from the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Up until then, there were no problems, particular problems. There were small provocations, and the soldiers even opened fire on a number of occasions, but there was no combat. There was no firing towards our units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So you're saying there was no firing towards your units but soldiers were opening fire. What were they opening fire at?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Usually this happened in the evening hours, when the soldiers were more fearful and on several occasions they announced that they had heard something and that they opened fire. This was more so on the Zdravec position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you testified that you didn't see any trenches, any bunkers, or any other fortifications in Ljuboten prior to the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Correct. There were no fortifications by the villagers or the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be fair to say, Mr. Grozdanovski, that you didn't see anything in Ljuboten leading up to the 12th of August that would have led you to believe there was a NLA presence in the village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: I underscored several time that we noticed movements in the night hours, late in the night, we saw horses on the road that leads to the Bacilas, to the sheepfolds, and to Matejce. The diary probably has an entry where the army reports about such movements in the time-period while we were on that position. Also, it was evident that so much movement occurred in a village after midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Perhaps I could refer you to the first suspect interview that you gave on the 30th of July, 2004. And could you please turn to tab 2, Mr. Grozdanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this is 65 ter number 1228.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And towards the back of that, Mr. Grozdanovski, you should find a Macedonian interpretation. There are only certain segments of the interview that have been interpreted at this time due to time constraints. And in the English version, would you please turn to page 16, and that is page 16 also in the Macedonian. Now, if you look approximately halfway down your page in the Macedonian, Mr. Grozdanovski, and it's also approximately halfway down in the English, you will see a question from a TK starting "now, Mr. Grozdanovski..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the question that's asked is: "Now, Mr. Grozdanovski would you explain to us about the general security situation in the area of Ljubanci-Ljuboten, since you and your unit was deployed there before the events in Ljuboten occurred." And you answered: "I can assess them as good. We did not have any problems on the part of the village of Ljuboten, if we can exclude the problem that they wanted to let their cows graze where our positions were. We did not allow them. They were not my positions. They were positions of the 2nd Company. I don't know about some other problems." You were then asked was there any fighting, riots, events, shootings since the time you were here and since the events happened on that weekend, 10 to 12 August, was there any sort of event. You then answered no. You were then asked: "I guess because it was the nature of your business to assess the area of the nature or the areas surrounding you, did you see any sort which would indicate any NLA presence in the area to you?" You answered: "At Zdravec -- from Zdravec where the observation point was located, several times they reported that they have seen people coming from the woods into the shepherds cottages, into the Bacila." You were then asked: "Ljubotenski Bacila?" And your answer is: "Yes, but there were no fights." Now if we can turn on in the English to page 18. It is also page 18 in the Macedonian. And to continue on from there. This is about a third of the way down the page. Do you see a question from TK saying: "Good, so you had information from your side." Do you see where that point is, Mr. Grozdanovski? This should be closer to the top of the page, about a third of the way down, I believe, if you're on page 18.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I have page 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are you looking at the second question on that page, asked by TK?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will read it in the English and you can tell me whether this matches what have you in front of you. The question is asked: "Good, so you had information from your side about possible movement from Matejce but what about Ljuboten." Do you have that in front of you, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And then it continues on: "Did you monitor any sort of activities prior to the incident in Ljuboten in the village of Ljuboten." And you answered: "We observed unusual movement of cars, unusual number, big number of cars, during the night as well unusual number of cars for a village and no other things." You were then asked: "I guess from your observation point you had a very good view over the village." And you answered: "From Smok the view was best." You were then asked about combat fortifications and preparations, and as you testified you answered there that you hadn't seen any such things. You were then asked: "Did you see any other signs or presence of NLA or strongholds, any sort of flags, graffiti or other markings. And you answered: "There flags on the mosque, but no other things." Next question was: "What else is interesting for us to ask you, this movement in the night, was it individual persons or was it a group of persons or horses used or something else?" Your answer was: "Like I said, many cars were travelling from the village to the city. In Macedonia it is unusual at 2.00 a.m. 20 cars would leave the village." And the final question that I will cover on this point was: "Was any activity taken from your side, because of this monitoring of the events? Did you record a number of the plates, did you inform the police, and did the police check these people? Did you check that?" And your answer was: "No, we didn't have such competences. Since it was really peaceful, we didn't pay any attention. It was only striking and it was not endangering us. Now, did you follow all of that, Mr. Grozdanovski? Sorry, were you able to follow that, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I followed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And would be it fair to say that there's no mention here of any ammunition being found?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The ammunition was found by the scouts that during the day moved in the regions where we didn't have soldiers. So the scouts were made up from the soldiers from the 1st Company, from Major Mario, and when they were coming back they found ammunition from Chinese production. We went to a meeting with Major Despodov when lieutenant Jurisic Mario was reporting on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation but my question is something a little bit different. My question to you is, is there any mention in your suspect interview about this ammunition being found?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as can I see, it is not mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And as far as you can see, was there any mention of the movement of horses?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I think there was a mention of it in one paragraph. It was explained in one of the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if can I take you back to that paragraph and this is just back over the page, the bottom paragraph and you were asked: "This movement in the night was it individual persons, was it a group of persons, were horses used or something else?" And then your response you only refer to cars. So would it be fair to say that you don't make any mention of horses being used for transportation for these sorts of goods around Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the movement of cars you've described, isn't it the case that in your view this was nothing more than something that was interesting, but you didn't see it as something that was a danger to you or something that was indicative of NLA activity?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI
utterances.text: The movement of the cars was not dangerous for us, but it was just an indication that something was happening in the village, that there was some activity. The cars did not move in our region but they were moving along the road from the village Ljuboten towards Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn --.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- we have, I believe, reached a point where we need to adjourn. Is this a convenient point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, Your Honour. I thought it was 1.00, so this is a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must adjourn now for the balance of the day and ask the witness to return tomorrow. We resume the hearing in another courtroom at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
